ROLE: For every live session recompute the interest mask from its state and queued output, register a session that has no registration yet, and drop the registration of a completed one, so that queued output always reaches an idle recipient and input is read exactly while the session may still accept it.

STRUCT.NAME: struct loop
STRUCT.ROLE: owns the epoll descriptor and borrows the broker registry

STRUCT.NAME: struct broker
STRUCT.ROLE: session registry iterated in index order

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: state, descriptor and queue that determine the mask

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: queue length that turns EPOLLOUT on and off

STRUCT.NAME: struct epoll_event
STRUCT.ROLE: registration record carrying the interest mask and the session pointer

FUNC.NAME: session_close_immediately
FUNC.ROLE: close a session whose registration cannot be updated

FUNC.NAME: epoll_ctl
FUNC.ROLE: apply EPOLL_CTL_MOD, falling back to EPOLL_CTL_ADD when the descriptor is not registered yet

VAR.NAME: EPOLL_CTL_MOD
VAR.ROLE: update of an already registered descriptor

VAR.NAME: EPOLLIN
VAR.ROLE: interest set while the session may still receive protocol input

VAR.NAME: EPOLLOUT
VAR.ROLE: interest set while queued output is non-empty

VAR.NAME: ENOENT
VAR.ROLE: epoll_ctl(MOD) reports it when the descriptor has no registration yet

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSING
VAR.ROLE: no read interest; write interest only while output remains

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSED
VAR.ROLE: no interest at all; the entry is about to be reaped

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: epoll_ctl
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int epoll_ctl(int epfd, int op, int fd, struct epoll_event *event)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 on success; -1 with errno set on failure (ENOENT when op is EPOLL_CTL_MOD and the descriptor is not registered, EBADF for a closed descriptor, EEXIST when adding twice)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrows the epoll_event for the duration of the call; the kernel stores only the mask and the data union, and the session pointer stored in data.ptr remains owned by the broker
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: ENOENT after EPOLL_CTL_MOD is expected for a descriptor registered no earlier than this call, so the caller retries with EPOLL_CTL_ADD; any other failure is logged and closes only that session, since a descriptor that cannot be armed can neither read nor write

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: broker_session_count
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: number of sessions currently in the registry (0 for NULL); a snapshot used as the loop bound of this iteration
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; sessions created later are handled by the next mask_sync call

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: broker_session_at
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: struct session *broker_session_at(const struct broker *b, size_t index)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: borrowed session at index, NULL when out of range
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; valid until the next reap, so it is only used to build the registration record
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; NULL entries are skipped

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_state
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: current lifecycle state; SESSION_CLOSED for NULL
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; unknown states fall through to 'skip' so a session is never armed on a state the loop does not understand

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_fd
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the descriptor owned by the session, -1 when the session is NULL or already released it
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed descriptor number; the loop only registers it and never closes it (session teardown does)
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; -1 means the session is finished and is skipped

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_output
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: borrowed queued-output buffer (NULL only for a NULL session); len > 0 adds EPOLLOUT to the interest mask
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; only len is read here
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; NULL is treated as an empty queue

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_immediately
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; releases the queue, closes the descriptor once and sets SESSION_CLOSED
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases this session's resources; the loop still holds no session ownership, and broker_reap removes the entry later
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; closing a descriptor automatically removes its epoll registration, so no manual EPOLL_CTL_DEL is needed

LOGIC.INPUT: l: the reactor whose interest masks are refreshed (NULL, or a NULL broker, is tolerated). The registry is read through the broker API; nothing is passed in from a call site other than the loop itself.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If l == NULL or l->broker == NULL or l->epfd < 0, return. 2. n = broker_session_count(l->broker); for i = 0 to n-1: s = broker_session_at(l->broker, i); if s == NULL, continue. 3. state = session_state(s); fd = session_fd(s). 4. If state == SESSION_CLOSED or fd < 0, continue: the descriptor is already closed, its registration disappeared with it, and broker_reap removes the entry in this same iteration. 5. interest = 0. If state == SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT or state == SESSION_READY: interest |= EPOLLIN (both states may still deliver protocol input; a session that has not sent CONNECT yet must be able to do so). 6. out = session_output(s); if out != NULL and out->len > 0: interest |= EPOLLOUT (this is what delivers queued output to a recipient that sends nothing further). 7. If interest == 0 (a CLOSING session whose queue is drained), continue: it owes nothing more, and the reap that runs before the next wait closes it. 8. Build ev with ev.events = interest and ev.data.ptr = s, then rc = epoll_ctl(l->epfd, EPOLL_CTL_MOD, fd, &ev). 9. If rc == 0, the mask is applied; continue. 10. If errno == ENOENT, the descriptor has no registration yet (a session accepted in this iteration, or a descriptor number reused after an earlier close): rc = epoll_ctl(l->epfd, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, fd, &ev); if rc != 0, diagnose on stderr and call session_close_immediately(s) so the loop does not keep a descriptor it cannot observe. 11. If rc was -1 with any other errno (EBADF, ENOMEM, ...), diagnose and call session_close_immediately(s): a session that cannot be armed would silently stop working, so closing only that session is the isolated failure response. 12. Continue with the next index. Registrations are level-triggered; no EPOLLET, EPOLLONESHOT or edge machinery is used, so a descriptor whose bytes were not all consumed is reported again by the next epoll_wait.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. Post-state: every live session with readable input is registered with EPOLLIN, every session with non-empty queued output is registered with EPOLLOUT, no session in SESSION_CLOSED or with a released descriptor keeps a registration, and a session whose registration could not be applied was closed instead of being left unobserved.
INVARIANTS_USED: queued output must keep the descriptor registered for EPOLLOUT until len reaches 0, so an idle recipient still drains
EPOLLIN is armed exactly while the session may accept protocol input
closing a descriptor removes its epoll registration automatically, so a closed session never receives events
a failing registration is a per-connection failure, never a reactor failure
mod-then-add-on-ENOENT is the only registration state machine, so no per-session bookkeeping has to be kept in the loop
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: l is a live loop with an open epoll descriptor; the broker registry is stable for the duration of the call (no session is destroyed while iterating).
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: the kernel interest masks agree with the broker state: EPOLLIN iff state is AWAITING_CONNECT/READY, EPOLLOUT iff queued output is non-empty; no descriptor is registered twice (adding twice would fail with EEXIST and close an innocent session).
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; called between epoll_wait batches.
